{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The core risk-allocation provisions are in good shape: indemnification (§ 20), IP and data ownership (§ 14), limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), warranties (§ 19), insurance (§ 18), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), governing law and venue (§ 28), and the absence of minimum commitments (§ 2.1) all meet our preferred position, with only minor sub-elements short of ideal wording that we do not propose to redline.

The problems are concentrated in a cluster of Customer-burdening commercial terms that appear to have been inserted inconsistently with the rest of the document: an unlimited, no-notice Vendor audit right with remote system access (§ 22.1), a sole-source exclusivity obligation on us (§ 2.2), a Customer-side most-favoured-nation covenant (§ 7.2), uncapped liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day payable by us (§ 7.6), an eighteen-month no-hire (§ 12.4), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2), and the complete absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right in a three-year term with twelve-month auto-renewals. Several of these directly contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment, and § 2.1, which disclaims any purchase commitment — so deletion also restores internal consistency.

Six items sit in walk-away territory under the playbook. Redlines have been prepared for each deviation; the § 22.1 audit redline did not pass automated verification and requires manual drafting before it goes out.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 | Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems; walk-away. Redline pending manual verification. |
| Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Sole and exclusive provider for hosted analytics for the full term; fails fallback; contradicts §§ 2.1 and 12.3. |
| Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Open-ended MFN running against us; no product, time or comparison limits; contradicts § 12.3. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 | USD 25,000/day, uncapped, triggered by "any delay in providing a dependency"; fails preferred and fallback. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-way, 18 months post-termination, all Vendor employees, and an effective no-hire. |
| Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | § 8.2 | 180-day opt-out window exceeds the 60-day fallback; walk-away. Renewal pricing (§ 8.3) is favourable. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9.3 (cause-based rights only) | No Customer convenience right anywhere in a three-year term with 12-month auto-renewals; walk-away. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 | Full preferred position; indemnities are Excluded Claims under § 21.3, better than the 3× fallback. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 | Customer ownership of data and Deliverables; minor points on payment condition and sublicensing noted only. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with full carve-outs. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Consent-free Customer assignment; no change-of-control trigger operates against us. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 | Affiliates and contractors included; § 13.2 perpetual licence for paid-up Vendor Technology. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No field-of-use or competitive restraint; § 2.2 addressed under the exclusivity rule. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 | New York law, New York County courts, no arbitration; mutual escalation and injunctive carve-out. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 | No minimum, take-or-pay or forecast obligation; §§ 22.2–22.3 are true-ups, not penalties. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 | Six months' assistance at Order Form rates; 30-day data return; no fee-dispute withholding. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 | Services warranty for the subscription term; mutual, non-swallowing disclaimer in § 19.5. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | All required limits met; insurance expressly does not limit Vendor's liabilities. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 22.1 — Vendor audit rights.** Audits at any time, without notice, with remote access to our systems. No frequency limit, no notice, direct system access.
2. **§ 2.2 — Sole-source exclusivity.** Full-term sole and exclusive provider obligation with no category narrowing, no 12-month limit and no performance-based exit.
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** Open-ended, with no defined product or service, no time limit and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
4. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice.** Windows longer than 90 days are walk-away.
5. **Termination for convenience — absent.** No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term with auto-renewals.
6. **§ 7.6 — Liquidated damages.** Uncapped daily accrual for minor breaches approaches walk-away territory.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the prepared redlines** on §§ 2.2, 7.2, 7.6, 8.2 and 12.4, and insert a new § 9.4 (Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, consistent with the refund mechanic in § 10.2, and confirmation that Vendor has no convenience right).
2. **Manually draft and verify the § 22.1 audit redline** before it is sent — the automated proposal did not verify. Target: one audit per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site independent auditor, no remote access, with the existing §§ 22.2–22.3 cost allocation and confidentiality retained.
3. **Raise the internal-consistency point with Vendor.** Sections 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 conflict with § 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (no exclusivity, MFC, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment). Deletion is the cleanest reconciliation and should be presented that way.
4. **Fallbacks to hold in reserve:** exclusivity — a narrow 12-month category exclusivity terminating automatically on SLA or delivery failure; liquidated damages — good-faith equitable adjustment of the affected schedule in place of the daily amount; non-solicit — mutual, 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire; renewal — 60-day opt-out window.
5. **Note for the file (no action):** minor sub-elements short of preferred wording that we are not redlining — Deliverable ownership conditioned on payment of Fees (§ 14.2); contractor support rather than express sublicensing in § 13.2; "Fees" excluding the one-time implementation charge for cap purposes (§ 1.5); insurance cancellation notice qualified by insurer availability (§ 18.2); and the absence of a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder (§ 8.2).

We do not recommend signature until the six walk-away items are resolved."}
